Christianity & Buddhism
Begin with two early Buddhist discourses: suffering, craving, not-self and release. Read these particular texts closely; ask your neighbour which tradition and teachers they follow.
01 / BEGIN WITH THE CLAIMS
Suffering, the self and the hope of release.
Choose a question. Read both starting points. Then follow the study.
What is wrong with the world?
CHRISTIAN STARTING POINT
Creation groans under corruption; Christian hope looks toward its liberation.
Romans 8:19–23
EARLY BUDDHIST DISCOURSES
SN 56:11 identifies suffering, craving as its origin, its cessation and a path of practice.
SN 56:11The four noble truths
02 / READ IN CONTEXT
The texts behind the conversation.
The comparison above identifies a difference. Here, return to the document: follow its wording, understand its setting and distinguish the text from an interpretation of it.
Read the whole passage and what surrounds it. Identify who is speaking and who is addressed. Note what is affirmed, what is denied and what the text leaves unexplained.
Setting the Wheel of Dhamma in Motion
SN 56:11 · Thanissaro Bhikkhu
The four noble truths and the eightfold path. A Pali discourse in Thanissaro Bhikkhu’s translation; this collection is scoped to these early discourses, not every Buddhist school.
Read the passage in full, including the surrounding argument. Compare the wording with the claim in the reading desk and note where interpretation begins.
The Not-self Characteristic
SN 22:59 · Thanissaro Bhikkhu
The five aggregates are examined as impermanent and not-self. Do not reduce this passage to the slogan that people do not exist.
Read the passage in full, including the surrounding argument. Compare the wording with the claim in the reading desk and note where interpretation begins.
03 / CARRY THE CONVERSATION
Make the comparison a study.
How can a good God allow suffering?
God is sovereign and good; evil is real, and Christ is our hope.
If salvation is a gift, why do good works matter?
Justified by faith alone; renewed for a life of obedience.
Does the resurrection really matter?
Christ rose bodily. Our forgiveness and hope depend on it.
How do we defend the faith without becoming combative?
Christ is Lord; our witness should be truthful, gentle and clear.
LISTEN BEFORE YOU ANSWER
What would you want to ask next?
Start with the selected question: What is wrong with the world? Ask how your neighbour understands it before offering your answer.
